messages:
maria: Heads-up — yesterday's canary for model-v2 hit the autopause guard. Noticed a steady latency bump and token cost drift after 30% traffic. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/testcase/12345 :warning:
kevin: saw that. Do we know which guard fired first — latency or token cost?
sam: logs show p95 latency up ~220ms from baseline around 14:12, errors +0.3%. Token cost per request jumped ~12% (because responses got longer).
ilana: we've been discussing a single threshold per metric, but this use-case suggests a combined signal would be nicer — e.g. require latency OR error to cross + token-cost-to-cost ratio & persist for N mins.
maria: agreed. operators don't want noisy pauses for transient spikes. Proposal: introduce a "degradation_score" that weights p95 delta, error-rate delta, and token-cost delta, with a rolling 5m window and min duration 3m before pause.
kevin: sketch of the score?
ilana: something lightweight: score = 0.5 * norm(p95_delta) + 0.3 * norm(error_delta) + 0.2 * norm(token_delta). norm() maps relative change to 0..1 with soft caps. If score > 0.6 for 3m -> autopause.
sam: sounds reasonable. Need to be careful normalizing token_delta across quantized models and responses with structured outputs (many tokens but cheap). Maybe token_delta should be normalized to $-impact rather than raw tokens.
maria: yes — use per-model unit cost multiplier in the formula. That avoids raw token variance.
kevin: also want a config example for the rollout API and console UX. quick draft:
```json
{
  "guard": {
    "type": "composite_degradation",
    "window_secs": 300,
    "min_duration_secs": 180,
    "weights": {"p95": 0.5, "errors": 0.3, "cost": 0.2},
    "threshold": 0.6,
    "cost_mode": "dollar_impact",
    "stabilize_samples": 5
  }
}
```
ilana: For console: show current score, individual metric deltas, and a suggested action: "auto-pause applied — reduce traffic to 0% or rollback to model-v1" with a one-click mute for 15m. UX should show "why" link to the raw telemetry.
maria: +1. Also we need a signal that the autopause was triggered by cost pressure vs latency so SREs can prioritize. Add a label in the event payload: primary_cause = [latency|errors|cost].
sam: telemetry side: emit both raw metrics and the computed score as an event: rollout.guard_evaluation with fields: rollout_id, score, primary_cause, contributing_metrics[]. That lets ops build dashboards and alerts.
kevin: since this changes behavior, we should ship as opt-in feature flag default OFF for automated autopause, and default ON for console suggestions only. Add a rollout flag in the API: `autopause_enabled: false`
maria: agree. We'll also add a canary UI slider to shrink traffic by suggested step (e.g., -10% every 2m) instead of full pause. That reduces user surprise.
sre-bot: (incident-gen) Note: if autopause triggers, create incident draft with summary and attach last 15m of traces.
deploy-bot: canary 1802349876-model-v2 -> AUTO-PAUSED at 1802350050 (reason: composite_degradation, score=0.72, primary_cause=latency).
kevin: next steps: implement scoring function in telemetry service, add config to rollout API, console changes for visibility and suggested actions. I'll pick up API changes; sam take telemetry math; ilana take console mockups?
ilana: on it, will post mockups by EOD.
maria: thanks team — aim to have RFC PR by Thurs. :thumbsup:
